written.myAnswer: Biology connects with Physics through biophysics, which applies physical principles to living systems; with Chemistry through biochemistry, which studies the chemical substances and reactions of life; with Statistics through biometry, which applies statistical methods to biological data; with Geography through biogeography, which studies the distribution of organisms; with Economics through bioeconomics, which studies the economic aspects of biological resources; and with Computer Science through bioinformatics, which uses computing to store and analyse biological information.

Science is collaborative because specialists from different fields share knowledge and combine their expertise to address complex problems. For example, the Human Genome Project involved molecular biology, genetics, informatics and computer science; climate change research draws on atmospheric science, ecology, economics and sociology; cancer research involves oncologists, biologists, biochemists, geneticists, pharmacologists and statisticians; robotics and artificial intelligence involve computer science, engineering, mathematics, neuroscience and psychology; and space exploration brings together fields such as astrophysics, planetary science, engineering, biology and medicine.
